title: Interleaved TP+PP scale probe for multi-GPU throughput & p95 regression detection
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Run a focused, reproducible stress probe that exercises combined tensor-parallel (TP) and pipeline-parallel (PP) execution modes across 4- to 16-GPU clusters to measure steady-state tokens/sec, p95 latency under load, and automated regression detection thresholds. Goals: 1) characterize scaling inefficiencies introduced by inter-stage buffering and KV-cache pressure, 2) validate our regression detector on cross-node noise, and 3) produce a small suite of standardized scenarios for CI/perf gating. This ticket covers harness orchestration, workload parameterization (sequence lengths, batch compositions, kv cache hit ratios), deterministic sampling for p95 stability, and dashboards + alerts integration.
acceptance_criteria: Bench harness can run reproducibly on k8s and baremetal clusters across TPxPP configurations (4/8/16 GPUs)
Produce tokens/sec and p95 artifacts per run with stable statistical summary (median, p95 CI, sample count)
Regression detector flags >1.5x p95 change with low false positive rate on historical noise traces
Results pushed to perf-store and visible on perf dashboard; a small README documents running steps and reproducibility knobs
run_scenarios: mixed: random seq 128-2048, poisson inter-arrival to emulate burstiness
tech_notes: We will reuse the tensor-pipeline orchestration shim from infra/tppp-controller but introduce deterministic seeding for request interleaving to reduce variance.
KV cache warmup windows discovered in initial experiments cause p95 transients; plan to run a warmup phase and exclude first N seconds from the p95 window used by regression detector.
Network serialization overhead is significant for PP inter-stage RPCs; instrumented with per-stage timers and ct-prof traces to attribute overhead to comm vs compute.
